content.abstract:
Twenty Fifth Indian Antarctic Expedition 2006-2007
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 23, pp 299-319
Logistic Report
Lt. Col. Janardhan Rao
Indian Army (EME)
Logistics is an important constituent of any expedition. It is not 
possible to survive long in the most hostile environment of Antarctic without 
any support which is needed for survival. Indian Army team made the core 
of the logistics of the Indian research base in Antarctica. The logistics 
team in the present Expedition comprised of total 13 members from the 
Indian Anny consisting of one officer each from Electrical and Mechanical 
Engineers (EME) and Engineers (Engrs.) with seven other ranks from EME 
and three from Engrs. One Mason from Engrs was also part of summer 
component. The Officer in-charge of the Army team was overall responsible 
for the Logistics and was declared the Deputy leader of the Expedition at 
Maitri.
During the voyage, the complete expedition cargo was inspected and 
reorganized to suit the logistic plan. The induction of the team into Maitri 
was planned in phased manner over a period of 5 days. Soon, the summer 
activities commenced.
Immediately after reaching Antarctic shelf the schedule of shifting 
the expedition team members to Maitri station by Helicopters was carried 
out. In the initial sorties, scientists and their equipments were shifted for 
starting the short summer expedition to carry out various scientific activities.
Since fuel and construction stores were required on priority, the team 
concentrated on the tasks of making the newly inducted Canadian trailers, 
Pisten Bulley (PB) - 300 vehicles and Mantis Crane operational. Pumping 
of fuel from ship into storage tankers at the shelf and necessary stores were 
stacked into containers. At the shelf itself an Automatic Weather Station 
(AWS) of SASE was established.
At Maitri, handing and taking over of all stores, equipment and vehicles 
was carried out. The team got acquainted with life support systems including 
central heating system, water supply and power generation. Training on all

vehicles/equipment and introductory convoy exercises was given by 
XXIV-ISEA members.
The main tasks which the logistics team was assigned immediately 
after reaching Antarctica were as under: -
(1) Cargo handling operations involved loading/unloading operations from 
the ship involving unloading of 25 Container loads, 02 Half bins, one 
new vehicle-Pisten Bully 300 MB, one Mantis crane and pumping of 
300 K1 fuel from the ship and back loading into the ship 12 containers 
placed at the shelf by the previous expedition. Overnight unloading/ 
loading of cargo from the ship to the shelf and vice-versa under very 
unfavorable conditions with winds at 40 knots, to meet the deadline in 
prevailing conditions.
(2) Shifting of stores and fuel from the ship to the station: All the stores 
were properly stacked in to the container and the fuel into the 20 K1 
fuel tankers. The stores and fuel are transported on trailers/sledges 
towed by Pisten Bully vehicles from the Continental ice shelf to the 
station over a distance of 130 kms through one of the roughest and 
undulating icy terrain under extreme conditions of flesh freezing 
temperatures, gusting winds and blizzard weather conditions. Planning 
and execution of convoys which was a herculean task involving lot of 
courage. Total 13 convoys were made during the expedition out of 
which llwere mainly for transportation of fuel and essential stores, 
back loading of scrap and waste between Shelf and Maitri. Two 
convoys were made purely for scientific programs such as establishment 
and operation of ice core drilling camps far away from the station on 
the icy white desert. As convoys form an important part of the 
expedition and provide a totally different aspect of the expedition full 
of adventure, they have been separately described under the heading 
‘CONVOYS’.
(3) Maintenance of the station involved operation of various life support 
systems, waste management system and environmental cleanliness. 
Some of the tasks are:-
(i) Operation and Maintenance of station power generation 
complex. The station is equipped with a total of 12 generating 
sets of which 2 x 125 KVA generators and remaining are 08 x 
62.5 KVA generators for the station and 02x30 KVA generators

for convoys and field camps, all with a 3 phase 415 V, 50 Hz 
supply. At any point of time two generators are in operation to 
provide the required power supply. Any generator is put through 
a 100 hour continuous running cycle. A regular Maintenance of 
the machines is carried out after each cycle. A regular 
maintenance of the machines is carried out after each cycle. A 
dedicated member from the army team is deputed to maintain 
the generators round the clock.
